questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the highlighted word(s) in the given sentence.

Anybody can solve this problem **if he tried.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence uses the phrase **"if he tried"**, which is grammatically incorrect as it mismatches the conditional structure.
 
• This is a case of a first conditional sentence, which describes a possible future action and its result.
 
• In first conditional sentences, the correct structure is: **if + present simple, will/can + base verb**.
 
• Hence, the verb “**try**” should be in the present simple tense, and the subject should match in plurality with “**anybody**” (which is singular in meaning but allows neutral plural pronouns in modern usage).

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2 – "if they try"**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Anybody can solve this problem if they try."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Use of the pronoun **"they"** as a singular gender-neutral alternative is acceptable and widely adopted in contemporary English.
 
• The use of past tense "tried" incorrectly implies a second conditional, which would require "could" instead of "can".

questions.question:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1 (Defiant)**.

__
 
• The word **"Intractable"** means something that is hard to deal with, manage, or control; stubborn or unmanageable. (दुराग्रही, जिद्दी)

 
 
• **Example: **The intractable child refused to listen to his parents and threw a tantrum in the store.
 
 
 
• **"Defiant"** refers to someone who resists authority or refuses to comply with rules, often in a bold or rebellious way. (अवज्ञाकारी, विद्रोही)
 
 
• **Example: **The defiant student refused to follow the teacher's instructions and openly argued in class.
 
 
 
• Therefore, we can infer that **"Defiant"** is the correct synonym for **"Intractable"**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 (Defiant)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Proper** (उचित): Something that is appropriate or suitable in the circumstances.

 
 
• **Example:** She followed the proper procedure to submit her application on time.
 
 
 
• **Versatile** (बहुमुखी): Someone or something that is adaptable and capable of performing many functions.
 
 
• **Example:** He is a versatile actor who can play both comedic and dramatic roles effectively.
 
 
 
• **Compliant** (आज्ञाकारी): Someone who is willing to follow rules or agree to requests.
 
 
• **Example:** The compliant employee immediately adjusted her schedule to accommodate the manager’s request.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

It is __all one__ whether I go today or tomorrow.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"it is all one"** is an old-fashioned idiom meaning **"it makes no difference"** or **"it is the same either way."**
 
• Among the given options, the phrase that best captures this meaning is **"just the same"**.
 
• The expression “just the same” means **regardless of circumstances** or **without change in meaning or outcome**, which aligns perfectly with the sentence context.
 
• Options like **"together," "in one piece,"** or **"proper"** do not convey the intended idiomatic meaning and are therefore incorrect substitutes.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3 – "just the same"**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"It is just the same whether I go today or tomorrow."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Idiomatic expressions often lose clarity when interpreted literally, so substituting them requires understanding of context and usage.
 
• “It is all one” is now considered archaic and is typically replaced in modern usage by phrases like “just the same,” “it doesn’t matter,” or “it’s all the same.”

questions.question:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**goes the extra mile**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**goes the extra mile**" means to make a special effort or to do more than what is expected, especially to help others. (अतिरिक्त प्रयास करना)
 
• The sentence describes a habitual action by the mother in helping people, which fits perfectly with this idiomatic expression.
 
• Other options are incorrect in this context: 
 
 
• **Turns a deaf ear**: Means to ignore someone – opposite of what the sentence implies.
 
• **Takes a rain check**: Means to postpone an invitation or offer – contextually irrelevant.
 
• **Breaks the bank**: Means to spend too much money – not suitable here.
 
 

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *My mother always goes the extra mile__ to help people.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Idioms enrich language** and convey meanings beyond the literal sense. Recognizing context is key to selecting the correct idiom.
 
• "Go the extra mile" is often used to describe people who are generous, dedicated, or caring.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Universal high-quality education is the best way forward for developing and maximising our country's rich talents and resources for the __good in the individual__, the society, the country and the world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2 – "good of the individual"**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"for the good of"** is a standard idiomatic expression meaning **for the benefit or welfare of someone or something**.
 
• In the sentence, the intended meaning is that education serves the benefit of various entities — **the individual, society, the country, and the world**.
 
• Hence, the correct structure is: **"for the good of the individual"**, not “for the good for/on/by.”
 
• “Good of” is always used with reference to a beneficiary, and is commonly seen in expressions like *“for the good of mankind”* or *“for the good of the community.”*

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2 – "good of the individual"**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Universal high-quality education is the best way forward for developing and maximising our country's rich talents and resources for the good **of the individual**, the society, the country and the world."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The expression “**for the good of**” is a fixed phrase in English and should not be altered unless the meaning or grammatical structure demands it.
 
• Other prepositions like “for,” “on,” or “by” after “good” would either change the meaning or render the phrase grammatically incorrect in this context.
 
• This phrase is widely used in academic, legal, and social discourse to indicate collective or individual benefit.

questions.question: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options.

options.text: It is too stranger to see a guy shouting in the mall without any reason.
It is too stranger to see a guy shout in the mall without any reason.
It is too stranger to see a guy shouting in the mall beside any reason.
It is strange to see a guy shouting in the mall without any reason.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Option 1: "It is too stranger to see a guy shouting in the mall without any reason."**

 
 
• This sentence is incorrect because "stranger" is a noun, not an adjective.
 
• The word "too" should be followed by an adjective, like "strange", not a noun.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: "It is too stranger to see a guy shout in the mall without any reason."**
 
 
• This sentence also misuses the word "stranger" instead of the correct adjective "strange".
 
• Although the verb "shout" is fine, the adjective use is incorrect.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: "It is too stranger to see a guy shouting in the mall beside any reason."**
 
 
• This sentence is incorrect for two reasons: misuse of "stranger" and incorrect preposition "beside" instead of "without".
 
 
 
• **Option 4: "It is strange to see a guy shouting in the mall without any reason."**
 
 
• This sentence is grammatically correct.
 
• “Strange” is a correct adjective, and the verb phrase “shouting in the mall without any reason” is contextually sound.
 
 

So, out of the given sentences, only Option 4 is grammatically and contextually correct.__

**Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 4".**

questions.question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.

options.text: Having belief in yourself is the big key to success.
Having belief in yourself is the most bigger key to success.
Having beliefs in yourself is the bigger key to success.
Having belief in yourself is the biggest key to success.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Option 1: "Having belief in yourself is the big key to success."**

 
 
• Incorrect usage of the adjective "big" in a context that requires a superlative degree.
 
• “The big key” sounds awkward; “the biggest key” is more appropriate when indicating something most important.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: "Having belief in yourself is the most bigger key to success."**
 
 
• Grammatically incorrect due to redundancy; “most” and “bigger” should not be used together.
 
• Either "bigger" (comparative) or "most big" (incorrect anyway) — not both.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: "Having beliefs in yourself is the bigger key to success."**
 
 
• “Beliefs” is plural, but “belief in yourself” is an abstract, singular idea — which is the intended meaning.
 
• Also, "the bigger key" implies a comparison between two, but no such comparison is made.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: "Having belief in yourself is the biggest key to success."**
 
 
• This sentence is grammatically correct and clearly conveys the intended meaning.
 
• Uses correct superlative form “biggest” to indicate the most important factor.
 
 

Therefore, Option 4 is the grammatically and contextually correct sentence.__

**Correct Sentence:** *"Having belief in yourself is the biggest key to success."*

• The sentence uses the phrase **"one of the"**, which must be followed by a **superlative degree** adjective to compare Jack with a group of people.
 
• Among the given options, **"the cleverest"** is the correct superlative form of “clever.”
 
• The use of **"most clever"** is also a superlative, but when a one-syllable adjective like "clever" has an "-est" form available, it is more natural and preferred in standard usage.
 
• Options like “clever” (positive degree) and “cleverer” (comparative degree) are not grammatically appropriate in this sentence structure.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2 – "the cleverest"**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Indeed, Jack is one of the **cleverest** men I have ever met."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Superlative adjectives are used with “one of the…” to show that someone/something belongs to a group characterized by the highest degree of a quality.
 
• Examples: “She is one of the **best** dancers,” “This is one of the **most interesting** books I’ve read.”
